name: Ada
want: a loom to weave our own cloth
does: Ada asked for a loom to weave cloth. She got the plans from a peddler—makes you wonder what else he was selling and who really sent him here, doesn't it? We've always bought our cloth, but I asked her all about the patterns she plans to weave. I built the frame so thick a runaway cart wouldn't dent it, and checked every joint twice just to be safe. No rush to finish it, though, we'll take it easy.
reasons: slide needs two values and a period
swing needs two values and a period

name: Corin
want: a windlass to haul the millstones
does: Lifts the millstones. Corin wants it, so I drew it. Why does he need a new one? The bench found the bar struck the top beam and drum, and the slide needed two values and seconds. I heard them. I set the slide to one unit and gave it four seconds. I lowered the bar so it stops below the drum. No ropes to break now, just a stout frame. If a stone falls, it falls. Worriers make too much of a squeaking timber. We have time.
reasons: slide needs two values and a period

name: Dunn
want: a strong wheel to stop the ice
does: Dunn says the ice is coming. A river freezing in summer? I've never seen it, but I take him at his word. He means well. The old wheel was useless, sat inside the posts and seized tight as a rusted bolt. Shoddy, idle work. I rebuilt it properly. The axle rests heavy on the posts now, bound under massive iron caps that could crush a boulder. It grinds true against the iron. Keep your hands clear of the caps when it turns, or it'll take your fingers. There's no hurry, but the work is done.
reasons: it would not stand: the cap_left and cap_right would tip over

name: Edek
want: a pump to pull the floodwater out
does: Pulls the worst of the floodwater out before it drowns the crops, if the timber holds. It'll throw a river's worth of water a day.
reasons: it would not pump: nothing in it turns against a load
drawing:
Those caps were just sitting loose on top of the spinning axle. No wonder they tipped right over! You can't just rest timber on something that turns and expect it to stay; the movement will throw it right off. I took them off and ran the iron axle straight through the posts instead, the way we build the wheels at the mill. It'll hold fast now. 

Are the fields very bad? How did Edek find out the water was rising so fast? I trust he knows what he's doing, but you have to be careful with floodwater—it'll wash away a weak footing before you even notice. Tell him to watch the banks. We should get this built quickly. There's no time to stand about when there's a river's worth of water to move, so I went ahead and fixed the drawing for him without waiting to be asked. Tobin and Gisla can help me cut the timber if we need it. How are you faring in all this wet?

name: Freya
want: a lever to lift the heavy stones
does: Freya asked for a lever for the quarry stones. I don't know why she's not using the ramps, but I take her at her word. The old drawing was broken, the joint didn't lift the load. I fixed it. Built a stout timber beam on an iron axle, with a basket at the end. Folks worry about the beam snapping. It's thick enough, and if a stone falls, just step back. No need to rush the work.
reasons: it would not stand: the basket_base would tip over

name: Gorm
want: a finer sieve to catch the grit
does: Gorm asked for a finer sieve, which makes me wonder who told him my milling leaves grit in the first place. I mended the slide and wove this cloth tight enough to catch the dust off a moth's wing, so it'll sift a mountain of grain. Take your time working it, but keep your fingers clear or that frame will pinch them clean off.

name: Ada
want: a loom to weave the storm
